testableA11yRules: Token contrast per design x mode (Classic light/dark, Airplane, Modern light/dark): composite any alpha tokens, then assert --fg, --muted, --ok, --warn, --err, detail, quantity, 'required' and placeholder tokens are >= 4.5:1 on every surface they are used on (bg, surface, lift); use no rounding (4.499 fails). Re-run under prefers-contrast: more with a >= 7:1 policy for body text.

UI boundary contrast: tick-box border, input border, toggle outline, checked glyph versus its fill, and focus ring are >= 3:1 against adjacent colours in every design/mode (Classic --lineStrong, Airplane --lineStrong, Modern --line). Decorative hairlines (--line in Classic and Airplane) must not be the only edge of a control.

Text must not sit directly on the Modern gradient or grain except the screen title: assert every text node other than the title has an opaque ancestor background; for the title compute worst-case contrast at every gradient stop plus midpoints with grain at maximum opacity (>= 4.5:1, or >= 3:1 if 24px/18.67px bold or larger). Forbid --muted directly on gradient.

Target size at 320, 360, 390 and 430 px widths: every button, [role=button], input, switch, row and drag-handle replacement is >= 24x24 CSS px (hard fail) and >= 48x48 (project target; 44 minimum); adjacent targets have >= 8px gap; hit areas expanded with ::before do not overlap neighbouring targets.

Focus: Tab through every screen in every design; computed outline-style is never none, outline-width >= 2px (target 3px), focus colour >= 3:1 against adjacent pixels, and focused-versus-unfocused change >= 3:1; the focused element is not entirely covered by the Close/Done dock (document.elementFromPoint at its centre and corners resolves to it or a descendant).
Drag alternative: every reorderable point has single-tap up/down (or move-to) controls and a keyboard path; verify without any pointermove events.

Pointer cancellation: pointerdown on a tick row or button does not change state; state changes on click only; pointerdown then moving > 10px outside the target then pointerup does not toggle; rapid double and triple taps on tick, Done and Save fire exactly once each (or toggle predictably) and sound/speech do not double-fire.

State not by colour alone: pending, done, skipped and required each expose a non-colour cue in the DOM (SVG glyph, word, shape) plus aria-checked or accessible name; a screenshot under html{filter:grayscale(1)} shows distinguishable checked and unchecked boxes in all three designs.

Reduced motion: with emulateMedia({reducedMotion:'reduce'}) document.getAnimations() has no running transform/translate/scale/rotate animations and no infinite iterations, press and tick states still change instantly; with the in-app Reduce effects on, the same holds, grain is display none and shadows are flat.

Forced colors: with emulateMedia({forcedColors:'active'}) the check mark is visible (screenshot diff checked vs unchecked), a focus outline renders, Modern shadows are not relied on, and grain/gradient layers are hidden.

Theme persistence and first paint: set stored design and mode, reload with the opposite emulated colorScheme, and assert documentElement.dataset.design and .mode are correct before first paint (MutationObserver from the inline head script); 'System' mode follows a live colorScheme change; with Storage.prototype.getItem and setItem throwing the app still renders a valid default (Classic, System).

Settings control itself: the Design/Mode selector, toggles and Left-handed switch meet the contrast, 48px and focus rules in each of the three designs, and the active design is exposed via aria-checked or aria-current plus visible text.

Layout invariants across designs: switching design changes no element order, stack direction (first item at the bottom, growing upward), checkmark side (right) or bounding-box positions of Done/Close by more than the shadow offset; document.documentElement.scrollHeight <= innerHeight on all screens except the references inner list (verify no body scroll, only .refs scrolls).

Reflow and text spacing: at 320x568, with the WCAG 1.4.12 override (line-height 1.5, letter-spacing .12em, word-spacing .16em, paragraph spacing 2x) and root font-size at 200 percent, there is no horizontal page scroll, no clipped text (scrollWidth/scrollHeight versus client sizes on overflow:hidden containers), and every action (tick, Done/Close, Save/Cancel) stays reachable via an inner scroller.

Safe areas and viewport: viewport meta includes viewport-fit=cover, shell height uses 100dvh, and dock padding uses env(safe-area-inset-bottom/right); bottom-right controls are not under the iOS home indicator (emulated insets of 34px bottom).
Status messages: a role=status (polite) region updates on tick, skip, and complete; tick sound and spoken confirmation stay off unless enabled per checklist; no auto-playing audio.

Inputs: all text and number inputs have computed font-size >= 16px; Ask number input has inputmode=numeric and handles empty, 0, negative, decimal, very long and pasted non-numeric values without throwing or showing NaN; Yes/No buttons are >= 48px.

axe-core (tags wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21aa, wcag22aa) reports zero violations per design x mode; every color-contrast 'incomplete' on gradient or grain surfaces must be covered by the token-level checks above.

Undo toast: Undo is a >= 48px button, the countdown pauses on focus and touch, it does not vanish while focused, it is reachable by screen reader, and a persistent 'Undo last' control exists; the toast does not cover the Done button.
openQuestions: Should Airplane be dark-only (my recommendation, matches the cockpit look) or also offer a light/day variant, and should it get a dim 'night' variant for dark rooms? The research says displays must be dimmable but gave no numbers.

Cockpit authenticity is unverified: the research found no hex values, and how Airbus ECAM draws completed lines (tick, recolour or cleared) and how Boeing 787 ECL draws overridden items are unconfirmed. The white-pending/green-done convention is only supported by Boeing ECL patents and MIT notes. Is 'cockpit-inspired' acceptable, or must it be provably authentic?
Does B612 Mono have a slashed or dotted zero and what is its advance width? Not verified; check the rendered font at 320px before fixing label lengths.

Is the Modern up-left hard shadow better than the conventional down-right for a right-thumb layout? It is an inference (avoids edge clipping and thumb occlusion) and should be A/B tested on real phones.

Do the SVG-grain values (180px tile, baseFrequency .8, numOctaves 2, about 8-10 percent effective strength) render without blank tiles, seams or scroll hitches on iOS Safari and mid-range Chrome Android? WebKit bugs 278813 and 287982 were seen only as search summaries; no benchmark exists. A PNG/WebP tile or no grain is the fallback.
Should hiding not-yet-reached items be offered at all? One-thing-at-a-time is folklore in the ADHD literature; default is to show the full stack with the next item emphasised.
Classic uses the system font, but the brief says fonts only from Google Fonts. I kept system-ui because it is the current look; confirm that is acceptable, otherwise Inter is the closest swap.
Should Left-handed mirror ship in the first pass? It is supported by medium-confidence statistics (67/33) and doubles the layout test matrix.
The effect of grain and gradients on ADHD or dyslexic readers is untested; the only mitigation is confining them to the background and offering a Grain/Reduce-effects switch. Is that enough?
Primary sources could not be read (WebFetch blocked); WCAG, Apple HIG, Material and Hoober wording came from search summaries, so exact figures should be rechecked when network access allows.
